items.title: No crate in this workspace is published to crates.io, so the first publication is undecided

must_fix.evidence: cargo info for all seven crates says 'could not find ... in registry'. There is no published baseline, so no release can be made and no pre-publish gate has a version to check against.

items.evidence: Measured 2026-10-27: `cargo package -p bevy_emerge_core` fails before any decision is reachable — "all dependencies must have a version requirement specified when packaging: dependency `bevy_emerge_rng` does not specify a version" (the `path` spec is dropped and crates.io is consulted). `bevy_emerge_solver` and `bevy_devshot` are also `publish = false`, so the graph has an unpublishable node in the middle. Making the workspace publishable is therefore: add a version to every intra-workspace path dependency (core->rng, core->solver, snip, anim, mapper->core/rng/solver/devshot, mcp->core), decide whether solver/devshot ship at all, then publish in dependency order rng -> solver -> core -> snip -> anim -> devshot -> mapper -> mcp. Until then the README's 'use the crates by path or git' is the only install path that works, and it is accurate. `bevy_elements` is a separate repo and already published (0.5.3, now 0.6.0).

items.evidence: target/loop/2026-10-22-fcc4e02/live (editor.log); /tmp/emerge_live/it9/probe_pin.py. Pointer investigation 2026-10-22 (CiBuilder): placement at scale 1 and 2 lands under the pointer (crates/bevy_emerge_mapper/tests/a_piece_lands_where_the_pointer_is.rs, 930ced5). Reproduced 2026-10-30 (bevy_emerge_w4, #182): a click on the door strip's 'the kit door' cue placed lamp_tall@4 at (-17.69, -2.69), off a 10 m map and off screen. Cause: view::cursor_ray handed a pointer outside the map camera's viewport (the frame's hole) to Camera::viewport_to_world, which extrapolates past the edge. Fixed: cursor_ray answers None outside camera.logical_viewport_rect(). Regression: tests/a_click_outside_the_viewport_places_nothing.rs (failed before: a click above the viewport placed wall@1 at (-20.5, -20.5)).

items.title: Notes for agents: a person marks tiles or meshes with a note, an agent works it, and the sign goes away
items.goal: A person selects one or more tiles or placed meshes and leaves a note for an agent. The note stands in the viewport as a small 3D construction sign; clicking it opens the note to read and edit. An agent lists open notes over MCP, does the work through ordinary operations and resolves the note, and its sign disappears while the change it made stays on screen. Resolved notes stay on record, so what has been worked can still be read.
acceptance: a note left on two placements and one tile is saved with the map's project and survives an editor restart
each open note shows one construction sign above its targets, and a resolved note shows none
clicking a sign opens its note; an edit to the text is saved and is one undo step
an agent over MCP lists the open notes with their targets, makes the change, resolves the note naming the operations it ran, and the sign is gone within a second while the change is on screen
resolved notes are listed with what resolved them, and an undo of the resolve brings the sign back
items.evidence: Owner's request 2026-10-28, with the focus in docs/loop/focus.md. Design defaults, so no pass has to stop for them: notes are data in the game's project beside the map they mark (one file per map, written like the map, hot-reloaded through bevy_emerge_core::live::FileWatch); a note has an id, its targets (placement ids and cells), its text, open or resolved, and on resolve the operation ids and one line of what changed; the sign is orange and white, about knee height on the map's scale, standing above the centre of its targets and never hiding them; every note change is a registered operation with undo, reachable from both the UI and MCP. The sign starts as a mesh built from Bevy primitives; a golem-made .glb replaces it only when the owner supplies one (AGENTS.md: meshes come from golem, not from this repo). A new keys::Action needs a row in the protected keys.rs census (see S3.7): ship click and button entry first and log a key as blocked rather than editing the census. 2026-10-28: moved to GitHub issues #89-#95 (label `owner`), which the owner approved as the plan and which extend it: drag a rectangle or Shift-click pieces, a box at the selection, Send, any MCP agent claims with a lease, a fence of area plus one cell, ask-first rules, review with Keep or Undo this note, and every note's history. Work the issues, not these steps; S4.1 stays the core they extend.

steps.evidence: 2026-10-28: a new registered operation needs a UI row (tests/operations_have_two_front_ends.rs::every_operation_has_a_ui_entry_point_and_the_other_way_round reads ops::UI_ENTRY_POINTS and requires the place string in editor/chooser/tiles/screen source). The editor has no selection and no text-field path for notes yet (that is S4.4), and the only existing person-side route is a key: a new keys::Action needs the Context::Map count and action list in keys.rs's #[cfg(test)] block raised, which is protected. Owner decision needed: either allow S4.4's panel/click UI to land together with S4.2 (a mouse path with no new Action), or an evaluator pass raises the keys.rs count for a note key. Design when unblocked: note_add/note_edit/note_resolve/note_reopen each read and write <map>.notes.ron through bevy_emerge_core::notes (path_for_map), inverse = same op with a `restore` of the whole Notes (only_as_undo), state = the Notes value; emerge_state gains notes (open with targets, resolved with ops and summary). 2026-10-28: moved to #89 (write a note) and #90 (list, history, send).
